Description: Players develop and establish shared naming conventions for objects and actions (like using a light bridge to "catch" a player or object).
Players use metonymic references as shorthand (like "orange" instead of "orange portal").
Players must pragmatically negotiate speaker reference frames when making and resolving spatial references like "keep going left".
Players use ad-hoc abstractions to refer to complex sequences of actions (e.g., "do the same trick" to refer to a sequence of actions).
Players construct subdialogues to seek and provide clarification multimodally.
A player can infer the necessity for clarification based on minimal information from their interlocutor (e.g., hesitation and saying "Uh." suffices).
Players can use in-game actions like shooting the portal to gesture at objects in conjunction with deictic utterances.
Players use metonymy and spatial references to refer to objects and actions in the game world.
